report.summary: The connected blue-gray house, burgundy gable, cream addition, and mustard service wing form a coherent miniature, but the most recognizable DQ sign and main roof silhouette are not yet convincing.

orientation.summary: The door inventory agrees with the geolocated views and labeled faces: SV1 supports the house/retail side entry on +u (SE); SV3 shows the highway-facing +v (SW) shop frontage; and SV4 shows the raised mustard-wing service door on -v (NE). The +v shop door and +u house door serve distinct volumes rather than duplicating one principal portal.

issues.problem: The prominent upright blue DQ rooftop sign from SV2 is rendered as a large dark, roof-like slab, while the readable DQ mark appears on an invented horizontal fascia.
issues.fix: Make the rooftop element an unmistakable upright blue sign with a pale base and readable DQ branding; reduce or remove the competing fascia logo.

issues.problem: The blue-gray house’s characteristic steep, narrow front-gabled silhouette in SV3 is diluted by an overly broad facade and a confusing pileup of intersecting roof masses.
issues.fix: Emphasize the tall front gable and simplify/lower the surrounding roofs so the house profile reads clearly from +v and in overview.

issues.problem: The shop and entry additions are overly blank and boxy compared with the vents, trim, steps, patio edge, and service character visible in SV2 and SV4.
issues.fix: Add a few bold miniature-scale details—gable trim, wall vent, raised steps/landing, and a compact patio cue—without chasing exact counts.
